title: DNA-PK-dependent RPA2 hyperphosphorylation facilitates DNA repair and suppresses sister chromatid exchange

grounded.evidence_quote: RPA2 is differentially phosphorylated during the cell cycle and in response to DNA damage.

grounded.source: genotoxic stresses that cause high levels of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs)
grounded.evidence_quote: In this study we demonstrate that RPA2 hyperphosphorylation occurs primarily in response to genotoxic stresses that cause high levels of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and that the DNA-dependent protein kinase complex (DNA-PK) is responsible for the modifications in vivo.

grounded.context: human HEK293T cells, chromatin-bound fraction, 4 hours treatment
grounded.evidence_quote: Similar to PCNA ubiquitination, the phosphorylation of RPA2 was induced in response to HU, MMS, or HU, 4NQO, or CPT treatments, but not to γ-irradiation.
grounded.location: RPA2 hyperphosphorylation is induced by DNA damage associated with stalled DNA replication
